# Moldova TRAVEL SURVIVAL KIT

**Traveler Types Covered**: Budget/Luxury/Family/Solo

## 1. SIM CARD SOLUTIONS

**Purpose**: Obtain local mobile connectivity for data and calls.

| **Provider** | **Details** |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Orange Moldova** | Best overall coverage. 100 MDL ($5.50 USD) for 20GB + local minutes (14-day validity). |
| **Moldcell** | Strong city coverage. Prepaid "Cartelă" plans starting at 50 MDL ($2.80 USD). |
| **Moldtelecom (Unite)** | Often the cheapest but coverage can be spotty in rural areas. Great for high-speed data in Chisinau. |
| **eSIM (Airalo/Holafly)** | Airalo "Moldcell" plans: 1GB/7 days (~$4.50 USD). Convenient but more expensive than local SIMs. |

**Recommendations**: Buy a physical SIM at the Orange or Moldcell kiosks in the Chisinau Airport arrivals hall for the best value.

---

## 2. AIRPORT TRANSFERS

**Route**: Chisinau International Airport (KIV) to Chisinau City Center.

| **Mode** | **Duration** | **Cost** | **Booking** | **Best For** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Trolleybus #30** | 40-50 mins | 6 MDL ($0.33 USD) | Pay conductor on board | Budget travelers; stops at Central Square. |
| **Ride-hailing (Yandex/Bolt)** | 20-30 mins | 100-150 MDL ($6-8 USD) | App-based | Convenience and fixed pricing. |
| **Official Taxi** | 20-30 mins | 150-200 MDL ($8-11 USD) | Airport counter | Groups or travelers without data. |
| **Hotel Shuttle** | 25 mins | 200-400 MDL | Pre-arranged | Stress-free arrival. |

**Note**: Trolleybus #30 operates from 06:00 to 23:00.

---

## 3. CURRENCY EXCHANGE

**Current Exchange Rate**: 1 USD ≈ 18.00 MDL (Moldovan Leu)

| **Location** | **Why It's Best** | **Rates** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chisinau City Center** | Banks (MAIB, Victoriabank) on Stefan cel Mare Blvd offer very fair rates. | Excellent |
| **Currency Booths** | Non-bank exchange shops (Schimb Valutar) are everywhere; many have 0% commission. | Very Good |
| **ATM Withdrawal** | Convenient; use bank-affiliated ATMs to avoid high third-party fees. | Mid-Market |
| **Airport** | Only exchange enough for a taxi ($10-20); rates are 10-15% worse than the city. | Poor |

---

## 4. MUST-HAVE APPS

| **Category** | **App** | **Purpose** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Transportation** | **Yandex Go / Bolt** | The primary ride-hailing services in Chisinau. |
| **Navigation** | **Maps.me** | Excellent offline maps for rural hiking or wine regions. |
| **Food Delivery** | **Glovo / Straus** | Main apps for restaurant and grocery delivery. |
| **Communication** | **Viber / WhatsApp** | Locals and businesses prefer Viber for communication. |

---

## 5. MUST-TRY FOODS

🍽️ **Plăcintă** – *Traditional Pastry*
→ What: Thin layers of dough filled with cheese (brânză), potatoes, cabbage, or cherries.
→ Where: La Plăcinte (chain) or local bakeries.
→ Price: 25–60 MDL.

🍽️ **Mămăligă cu Friptură** – *Cornmeal Porridge with Meat*
→ What: Dense cornmeal mash served with pork stew, sour cream, and grated feta.
→ Where: Fuior Gourmet or Roata Vremii.
→ Price: 120–200 MDL.

🍽️ **Zeamă** – *National Soup*
→ What: A light chicken noodle soup made with homemade noodles and a sour fermented bran (borș).
→ Try with: Sour cream and hot peppers.

---

## 6. UNIQUE ITEMS TO BUY

| **Item** | **Why Worth Buying** | **Where to Buy** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Moldovan Wine** | World-class quality (Cricova, Purcari, Castel Mimi). | Wine shops or supermarkets. |
| **Divin** | High-quality Moldovan brandy (try the Kvint brand). | Specialized liquor stores. |
| **Traditional Wear** | "Iie" – Hand-embroidered linen shirts. | Art Market (Piata de Suveniruri). |
| **Ceramics** | Black pottery and traditional clay jugs. | Souvenir market near the National Theater. |

---

## 7. SUPERMARKETS

*   **Nr1 (Numele Unu)**: Best selection of international goods and fresh deli items.
*   **Linella**: Most common convenience-style supermarket; found in every neighborhood.
*   **Fidesco**: Reliable middle-ground with good wine sections.
*   **Metro**: Bulk buying, located on the outskirts of Chisinau.

---

## 8. MARKETS (Day & Night)

| **Market Name** | **Location** | **Best For** | **Tips** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Piața Centrală** | City Center | Fresh produce, local honey, and cheese. | Chaotic but authentic; watch your pockets. |
| **Art Market** | Stefan cel Mare | Souvenirs, antiques, and local art. | Bargaining is expected here. |
| **Calea Basarabiei** | Outskirts | Industrial goods, clothing, and household items. | Massive and best visited on weekends. |

| **Brand/Type** | **Flavor Profile** | **Where to Buy** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Fetească Regală** | Iconic white wine; crisp and floral. | Any wine shop. |
| **Purcari Negru de Purcari** | Premium red blend; Moldova's most famous export. | Specialized boutiques. |
| **Bere Chișinău** | Standard local lager. | Everywhere. |
| **Kvint (Divin)** | Smooth, aged brandy (try 5 or 10-year). | Official Kvint stores. |

## 10. BEST PUBS/BARS

*   **Invino**: Chisinau’s premier wine bar with expert-led tastings.
*   **Kira's Club**: Casual vibe, outdoor seating, and popular with the creative crowd.
*   **Barbar**: Upscale atmosphere that turns into a party spot on weekends.
*   **TapRoom 27**: The go-to spot for local craft beer enthusiasts.

---

## 11. LOCAL FESTIVALS & EVENTS
Moldova hosts the famous National Wine Day in October, featuring tastings from every major winery. Other events include Martisor in March, celebrating the arrival of spring with red and white trinkets.

---

## 12. CUSTOMS & ETIQUETTE

### 12a. Temple & Sacred Site Dress Code
Moldova is predominantly Orthodox Christian. Modesty is expected when entering churches.

| **Rule** | **What to Check** | **Enforcement Level** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Head covering** | Women usually wear a scarf. | Strict in monasteries. |
| **Knees/Shoulders** | No shorts or sleeveless tops. | Strictly enforced. |
| **Footwear** | Shoes stay on. | Standard. |

### 12b. Cultural Hierarchy
Respect for elders is paramount in Moldovan society. Always offer your seat on public transport to older individuals or pregnant women.

### 12c. Religious Etiquette
Do not take photos during active services. Speak in whispers and avoid walking between the priest and the altar.

| **Rule** | **Detail** | **Who It Applies To** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Service conduct** | Stand during the liturgy; no sitting. | All visitors. |
| **Photography** | Ask before filming monks/nuns. | All visitors. |

### 12d. Saving Face & Conflict Resolution
Moldovans are generally direct but highly value hospitality. Avoid criticizing local politics or the Transnistria situation unless you are with close friends.

### 12e. Responsible Tourism
Support local producers by buying wine and honey directly from villages. Avoid littering in the protected Orheiul Vechi landscape.

### 12f. General Social Customs
Remove shoes when entering a Moldovan home. If invited for dinner, bringing a small gift like flowers (odd numbers only) or sweets is expected.

---

## 13. SAFETY & PRACTICAL INFORMATION

### 13a. Vaccinations & Preventative Health
Standard European health precautions apply. Ensure routine vaccinations are up to date.

| **Vaccine** | **Priority** | **Notes** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hepatitis A** | Recommended | For food/water safety. |
| **Tick-borne Encephalitis** | Seasonal | For hiking in forested areas. |

### 13b. Mosquito-Borne Illness & Insect Protection
Mosquitoes are a nuisance in summer but do not carry major tropical diseases.

| **Disease** | **Risk** | **Prevention** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **West Nile Virus** | Very Low | Use repellent in evening. |

### 13c. Water & Food Safety
Tap water is generally not recommended for drinking; rely on bottled or filtered water.

| **Source** | **Safety** | **Guidance** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tap Water** | Low | Boil before use or buy bottled. |
| **Street Food** | High | High turnover stalls are safe. |

### 13d. Personal Safety & Crime Awareness

*   **Overall Safety Rating**: Moderate-High. Chisinau is generally safer than many Western European capitals regarding violent crime.
*   **Petty Theft**: Bag-snatching and pickpocketing occur in crowded areas, specifically the **Piața Centrală** and on crowded trolleybuses (Lines 22 and 24). Keep your valuables in front pockets or zipped bags.
*   **ATM & Credit Card Scams**: Use only ATMs located inside banks. "Skimming" devices are occasionally found on street-facing machines. Always cover your PIN.
*   **The "Dropped Wallet" Scam**: If someone drops a wallet in front of you and another "bystander" suggests sharing the contents, keep walking. It is a setup to accuse you of theft later.
*   **Transnistria Considerations**: This breakaway region is not under Moldovan government control. While generally safe for day trips, your embassy’s ability to assist you there is extremely limited. Always carry your passport, avoid photographing military checkpoints, and ensure you return before your entry permit expires.
*   **Police Interactions**: While corruption has decreased, some officers may target tourists for "document checks." Always carry a photocopy of your passport. If asked for a fine on the spot, insist on a formal receipt at the police station.

### 13e. Emergency Contacts

| **Service** | **Contact** | **Notes** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **General Emergency** | 112 | Police, Fire, and Ambulance. |
| **Tourist Police** | +373 22 253 333 | Chisinau specific assistance. |
| **US Embassy** | +373 22 408 300 | Located in Chisinau. |
| **UK Embassy** | +373 22 225 902 | Located in Chisinau. |
